subject: Competitive match request & tiering proposal — Nova Health
messages:
From: Emma Carter <emma@novahealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing inquiry: hosted per-token vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for the demo last week — team really liked the throughput numbers and the KV-cache behavior you showed. We're evaluating a switch for our conversational and vector search pipelines and need a straightforward price comparison to share with finance/procurement.

Quick background:
- Expected steady-state consumption (Q1-Q2): ~2.0B generation tokens/month (mixed length; ~30% long-form summaries) and ~400M embedding tokens/month.
- Current benchmark vendors: OpenAI (gpt-4.1-equivalent hosted) and Anthropic cloud endpoints. We're seeing blended per-token spend today of roughly $0.00037 per generation token and $0.00009 per embedding token (including some volume discounts and reserved commit).

Can Redwood provide:
1) A matched per-token price (or better) for a commit of ~2B gen / 400M embed per month, plus how you would tier that commit (breakpoints).
2) Overage pricing, ramp assumptions, and any short-term credits or onboarding discounts you can offer to make the economics work for our CFO.
3) Any constraints: maximum SLA, data retention options, and whether private deployment is required for any lower price points.

I attached our projection sheet (nova_projection_q4.xlsx) with the month-by-month ramp. We need an indicative commercial that I can push to procurement by end of next week.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Carter
Head of AI Platforms, Nova Health
emma@novahealth.com
--- Attachment: nova_projection_q4.xlsx (xlsx)
From: sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
To: Emma Carter <emma@novahealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing inquiry: hosted per-token vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Emma — appreciate the projection and the context. Short answer: we can match (and in several usage bands beat) the blended economics you shared, with a simple tiered commit and a one-time onboarding credit to offset migration costs. High-level proposal below — this is an indicative commercial (valid 30 days) and assumes standard Redwood Hosted terms (SOC 2, 90-day logs by default).

Proposed commit tiers (monthly committed usage):
- Tier 1: 200M gen / 50M embed — $0.00038 gen / $0.000095 embed
- Tier 2: 500M gen / 120M embed — $0.00032 gen / $0.000080 embed
- Tier 3: 2.0B gen / 400M embed — $0.00026 gen / $0.000065 embed (this is the band that matches/undercuts your blended numbers)

Overage and ramp: overage priced at Tier 1 rates until next invoice / true-up. We can include a 10% spike buffer for the first 3 months to accommodate bursty traffic; sustained usage above committed band would be rebilled at the next tier rate with 30-day notice.

Commercial sweeteners (one-off / limited-time):
- $25,000 onboarding credit (applied to first two invoices)
- Free assistance for initial prompts & evals (up to 5 engineer-days)
- 30-day price protection for signed commit (locks the rates above for 12 months)

Notes / requirements:
- If Nova requires 12-month audit/log retention (vs our default 90d), that will need a SKU adjustment (we can include pricing in the formal quote).
- For discount stacking to apply, we need a signed SOW + MSA.
- Please confirm expected ramp months (from your sheet) and whether embeddings will be co-located in the same region (us-east) — that affects egress and routing.

I've attached a draft quote (redwood_quote_nova_health_20261119.pdf). I looped in Ben for billing and Lauren for approvals on the discount band. If this looks directionally right I can ask Legal/Deal Desk to prepare a formal quote + DocuSign package.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwoodinference.com
--- Attachment: redwood_quote_nova_health_20261119.pdf (pdf)
